rules.title: Boston fair housing protection for rental assistance (source of income)
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against renters because they use rental assistance, such as Section 8, social security disability or veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is listed as an example of housing discrimination.
rules.key_value: Rental assistance (e.g., Section 8 vouchers) is a protected class
rules.quoted_span: In the City of Boston, it’s illegal to discriminate when renting, buying, selling, or securing financing for any housing.
rules.coverage_text: Renting, buying, selling, or securing financing for any housing in the City of Boston
rules.interaction: The Fair Housing Commission enforces local, state and federal fair housing laws. Complaints about discrimination outside Boston go to the state.
rules.extraction_note: This is an informational city web page, not the ordinance text. It gives no ordinance citation, effective or enactment date, exemptions or penalties. It says only that the commission investigates complaints and tries to resolve them. Source-of-income protection comes from 'Rental Assistance' in the protected-class list (with the footnote 'For example renters using Section 8 voucher') and from the example 'The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance.' No criminal-history screening rules are stated.
